⭐️ BlackRock wants tokenized funds to back traditional Wall Street trades 

📣 BlackRock has identified the use of tokenized investment funds as trading collateral in traditional financial markets as a potential next application for blockchain technology, building on existing arrangements that already allow institutional crypto traders to pledge tokenized fund holdings. Dan Maley, BlackRock’s head of cash management for Asia Pacific, said the firm’s tokenized funds are already being used as collateral in digital-asset markets. Extending that capability into conventional financial markets remains more complicated, although the asset manager sees opportunities for investors to transfer fund holdings without first redeeming them for cash.

🔔 The development moves BlackRock’s discussion beyond issuing digital representations of traditional investment products. Its focus now includes how those assets could function within the systems financial institutions use to settle transactions, secure trading positions and manage available cash. Collateral plays an established role in financial markets because banks, brokers and clearing firms require assets to secure loans, derivatives positions and other transactions. Investors commonly provide cash or eligible securities, with each receiving institution setting rules for the assets it will accept.

🔗 BlackRock sees a potential role for tokenized money market fund shares in that process. A tokenized share represents an interest in an investment fund while allowing certain transactions involving that interest to take place through blockchain infrastructure. In the Bloomberg interview, Maley described the opportunity to bring tokenized funds into the traditional financial ecosystem. He distinguished the collateral arrangements already operating in cryptocurrency markets from the more difficult work of connecting blockchain-based assets with established financial systems.

➡️From Vintage to MNTGE: Digital Fashion Brand to Release NFT Patches Linked to IRL Rewards

Digital fashion brand MNTGE is gearing up to release its Patchwork collection, comprised of a series of non-fungible token (NFT) patches paired with a physical counterpart.

MNTGE Patchwork features 13 unique digital patches designed by 11 artists including Jen Stark, Bored Ape Yacht Club artist Seneca and Nyan Cat meme creator Christopher Torres. The entire 7,500-unit collection will open for sale on July 27 on NFT marketplace OpenSea. Each NFT will be priced at 0.07 ETH, or $130, and the artwork will be revealed upon mint.

Each NFT is linked to an identical physical patch. Embedded with a near-field communication (NFC) chip, owners can scan the real-world patch to claim the digital token in their crypto wallet. By holding the patch on the blockchain and IRL, users can trace ownership as well as attend token-gated events and exclusive MNTGE experiences.

Additionally, the patches aren’t just one-off collectibles. In the physical world, they can be sewn onto MNTGE’s “base garments,” including t-shirts, jackets and denim. In the digital realm, the patches can be “owned” by the base garment itself. By implementing an ERC-6551 token standard, the digital wearable becomes a token-bound account that can custody the patches – creating an added layer of digital ownership.

Nick Adler, co-founder of MNTGE, told CoinDesk that the company was rooted in the goal of selling vintage fashion and utilizing the blockchain to revitalize its origins.

“People are out there wearing [vintage] and collecting it…young kids want to be authentic,” said Adler. “They don't want a Hot Topic shirt, they want the original shirt, right? So we just saw this natural, really honest use case for the blockchain, and we just felt like the two could really go hand in hand.”

🇷🇸"Brian! Who is behind the protests in Serbia?"

The short answer - it looks like the US. 

The longer answer... 

To actually, definitively answer this question, you need to look up the organizations involved directly in the protests, as well as the organizations supporting and promoting it legally, logistically, financially, and across information space politically.

I did this last year ( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HGaqIPhCtY0 ) during similar protests and it is almost certainly the same case this year - this is a rerun.  

I'm surely not the only human being on Earth that can look these things up, but since many have asked, I have begun looking this year as well. 

This requires research that can take several hours of dedicated focus to answer. 

To start, look at US government-funded media like Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty or British state media like BBC and see how they're spinning it. 

If they are enthusiastically promoting it - it is almost CERTAIN it is US-backed. 

If they are decrying it as "anti-democratic mobs" or "Russian/Chinese meddling" it is almost CERTAIN it is aimed at dismantling US-backed proxies/parties/programs. 

Regarding the current protests in Serbia - in just a few minutes I have found several organizations in the middle of supporting them funded by the US/EU governments including:

1. ACLED (Armed Conflict Location & Event Data Project) ( https://npr.org/2026/10/24/nx-s1-6012799/european-student-protests-take-aim-at-serbias-elections );
2. The Global Resilience Fund ( https://theglobalresiliencefund.org/serbiaprotests2025 );

No, "legit" protests don't get hijacked - that's not how the US has ever operated - large protests require years of preparations and network building. If the US is involved it is because they are behind it. 

To everyone who will message me saying "No! the current government is horrible, this is legit protests!" 

No matter how bad you "think" your government is, the US-backed puppets they will replace it with will be 10000x worse - just ask Ukraine. 

If you are going to tell me the protests are legit - you need to show me the special interests that are behind the protests and show me a list longer and more convincing than the one I showed above. 

And no - protests are never "decentralized" - this is simply the US doing a better job covering its tracks. ALL protests - good or bad - have special interests (good or bad) behind them. Human beings do not spontaneously self-organize on this sort of scale.

AI could turn out to be both the greatest technological revolution of the past few decades and one of the biggest investment bubbles in history.

Yesterday, Anthropic reported a net loss of $80.7 billion in just the first half of the year. To be fair, there’s no need to panic over the headline number itself. Around $72 billion of that loss came from an accounting revaluation of the company’s liabilities, not from Anthropic actually burning through that much cash. But something else is far more interesting.

The company has already committed hundreds of billions of dollars to computing capacity, chips, and data centers. And Anthropic is far from alone. Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Meta are set to invest more than $700 billion in AI infrastructure this year. The scale has become so enormous that these investments are now supporting the U.S. stock market and accounting for a significant share of investment activity across the economy.

And this is where the U.S. is gradually falling into a very interesting trap. If tech companies keep spending at this pace, they’ll have to borrow more and more money and somehow prove that these massive investments will actually pay off. If they start cutting spending, the fallout will hit chipmakers, data centers, the energy sector, the tech companies themselves, and ultimately the stock market.

In other words, the AI boom is becoming too big to simply bring to a halt without serious consequences. The IMF already estimates that a sharp pullback in AI investment could leave the U.S. economy around 1.8% smaller by 2028 than it would be under the current baseline scenario.

Anthropic’s IPO in November could become the first serious test of this whole setup. Not long ago, the market was discussing a valuation of around $2 trillion for the company. Following the latest figures, some investors are now talking about roughly $1.5 trillion. At the same time, the business itself continues to grow at an extraordinary pace.

From a capital markets perspective, I see the main risk here as something other than AI itself. I have little doubt that it will fundamentally reshape the economy and the world. But the gap between the hundreds of billions being invested today and the point at which those investments start generating comparable returns could be much longer than the market currently expects. That’s precisely where the risk of today’s euphoria lies. Major technological shifts almost never happen quickly or without friction.

👀 Five journal metrics that reveal what drives results

Profit, win rate, payoff ratio and drawdown don’t tell the whole story. These breakdowns show where your strategy works—and where decisions get in the way:

🟢 Holding time: See which trade duration suits your style.

🟢 Winners vs. losers: Compare holding times. Are you taking profits too soon, holding losses too long, or keeping winners past the setup?

🟢 Results by session: Find when you trade best. Look for patterns, but don’t change your schedule based on one result.

🟢 Market conditions: Check whether you perform best in trending or ranging markets—and whether those conditions are present.

🟢 Position size: Compare results at different sizes. Larger positions affect mindset and risk; size up only when the setup and conditions support it.

Track useful breakdowns consistently, not every stat. Use patterns to find your edge, improve habits and choose what to focus on next.
